clue.text: The age of the ass lasting a long time

definitions.meaning: read literally, the years a donkey (an ass) has lived
the idiom for a very long period, as in 'I haven't seen her for ages'

explanation.surface: A musing on how long a donkey lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an extremely long stretch, and literally it is a donkey's lifespan; an ass is a donkey.

clue.text: Lace bed in state of collapse

indicators.note: a bed in a state of collapse has its letters fallen into disorder, signalling the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A lace-covered bed has fallen down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in state of' signals rearranging LACE and BED into the seven letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden failure or ruinous breakdown.

clue.text: Not a perfect service; all the players catch it

definitions.meaning: in tennis a serve that clips the net is faulty
a team sport where every player passes by catching the ball

explanation.surface: A tennis serve goes wrong and everyone grabs the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer as two words: a served ball that hits the net.
explanation.definitionFit: A serve striking the top of the net is imperfect; the court game played mostly by women is built on catching passes.

clue.text: Impromptu arrangement of extreme little Latin work

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: op. is the short form of opus, Latin for a work

explanation.surface: An unrehearsed setting of an extreme short Latin composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement of' shuffles EXTREME together with OP (opus).
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something done without preparation, on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: Brown cuttlefish

definitions.meaning: a reddish-brown colour, as in old photographs
the genus name of the common cuttlefish

explanation.surface: A brown cuttlefish.
explanation.definitionFit: The reddish-brown pigment was originally made from cuttlefish ink, and the cuttlefish genus bears the same name.

clue.text: An extortioner offering precise alternative

parts.note: exact means precise
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A blackmailer presenting an accurate alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: One who exacts, demanding money by force or threat, is an extortioner.

clue.text: West dame who has been booked

definitions.meaning: the title character of Daphne du Maurier's novel, a heroine put in a book

explanation.surface: A woman in the West who has made a reservation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' looks like a reservation but means made into a book: the du Maurier novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Rebecca West was a writer, and du Maurier's novel shares the first name as its title.

clue.text: Dog crating with unsubstantial sparring

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely, to shadow
crating goods is boxing them

explanation.surface: Putting a dog in a crate along with a bit of feeble fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer practising against an imaginary opponent spars with no substance in front of him.

clue.text: Initially a British industry that developed about environment

indicators.note: placed around the other letters, enclosing them
something developed has changed form, so these letters are rearranged
the first letters of the words a, British and industry are taken

explanation.surface: How a British industry first grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges THAT to HTAT, which goes 'about' ABI, the initials of 'a British industry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural home or surroundings of a plant or animal is its environment.

clue.text: It fuels fire of Irish poet wandering with extraordinary gab

indicators.note: a wandering poet strays about, so its letters move
extraordinary gab is gab out of its usual order

explanation.surface: An Irish bard roams about with remarkable chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals, 'wandering' and 'extraordinary', mix POET and GAB together.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf cut from bogland is the traditional Irish fuel, burnt on the hearth.

clue.text: He probably used a brush and a big rope

parts.note: great means big
a painter is the rope used to tie up a small boat

explanation.surface: An artist working with a brush and a hefty rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A master artist applies paint with a brush.

clue.text: Make a speech about decimal changes

indicators.note: the word decimal changes, its letters taking a new order

explanation.surface: Orating about the switch to decimal currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak rhetorically, as an orator does.

clue.text: A dry pain at work among Ambassador's staff

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Someone tired and teetotal suffering at an embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior diplomat assigned to an embassy works on the ambassador's staff.

clue.text: A revolutionary checked by railway spokesman

definitions.text: A revolutionary checked by railway spokesman

parts.words: A revolutionary checked by railway spokesman
parts.note: something that revolves, braked on rails, and carrying spokes

explanation.surface: A rebel caught by a railway press officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' is a thing that turns round and 'spokesman' something with spokes, not a rebel and a press officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating disc with spokes turns on a railway and is stopped by brakes.

clue.text: Old boy domestic taking notice

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a domestic is a household servant

explanation.surface: A former pupil working as a servant keeps an eye on things.
explanation.definitionFit: An attentive person who notices things is watchful.

clue.text: This time step gingerly over dying fire

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits over, above, the next
stepping gingerly means stepping carefully and awkwardly, so these letters are moved about

parts.note: an ember is a glowing remnant of a dying fire

explanation.surface: Stepping carefully over the last embers of a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gingerly' rearranges STEP to SEPT, placed 'over' EMBER. 'This time' means the present month for the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A month is a period of time; the clue speaks of the month in which the puzzle appeared.

clue.text: Be oblivious to rising alarm?

parts.note: an alarm clock meant to get you rising goes unheard, so you stay asleep too long

explanation.surface: Ignoring growing panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising alarm' sounds like mounting fear but is the clock that wakes you up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sleeps past the time set on the clock has slept too long.

clue.text: Rome bag tied up by prohibition …

indicators.note: something tied up in knots is tangled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bag from Rome held up by a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade is a prohibition.

clue.text: … but perhaps send round to create a Euclidean situation

indicators.note: sending letters round moves them about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sending something round to make geometry happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the previous clue; 'round' is the anagram signal and 'perhaps' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a line subtends an angle when it lies opposite it, a term from Euclid's work.

clue.text: Balkan city seat I get ensconced in

indicators.note: settled comfortably within, as one is in a seat

parts.note: a sofa is a seat

explanation.surface: Getting comfortable on a seat in a Balkan city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Bulgaria is a Balkan city.

clue.text: How aero-engine suddenly came to rest in a stable?

definitions.text: How aero-engine suddenly came to rest
definitions.meaning: an engine that cuts out abruptly has failed in flight
kept in a stall, as a horse is

explanation.surface: An engine stops and a horse is stabled.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft engine that cuts out has stopped; an animal kept in a stall is housed in a stable.

clue.text: Decorated earthenware is first-class in some garden enclosure

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a fence encloses a garden
A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: Fine pottery sits within a garden boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Glazed and painted pottery of this kind is decorated earthenware.

clue.text: Drinks booze, half-back coming round…

indicators.note: coming round means enclosing the other piece
back means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: semi- means half
to bib is to drink, to booze

explanation.surface: A footballer drinks while coming round after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-back' looks like a football position, but 'back' turns the word for half, and 'coming round' wraps that turned word around the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, especially alcohol.

clue.text: Was present at conference of lustrous stuff

definitions.meaning: to sit in on a meeting is to attend it

explanation.surface: A conference attended in shiny cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words: SAT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting in means attending; the glossy woven fabric is lustrous material.

clue.text: … for a case of high spirits?

definitions.text: … for a case of high spirits?

parts.words: … for a case of high spirits?
parts.note: continuing the drinking theme, a case of spirits drunk brings a happy glow

explanation.surface: Drinking for a case of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the drinker in the previous clue; 'case of high spirits' reads as a crate of liquor and as a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Great happiness and exhilaration are high spirits.

clue.text: Piece of clothing for men in Garters (not the Queen's)

indicators.note: not means the letters named are left out

parts.note: ER is the Queen's royal cipher, with the possessive S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clothing for men wearing Garters, but not the Queen's.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Queen's cipher (Elizabeth Regina); with its possessive S it is removed by 'not', and 'in' puts the men inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Any item worn on the body is an article of clothing.

clue.text: Equilibrium the spendthrift is apt to lose

definitions.meaning: a state of being evenly poised

definitions.text: the spendthrift is apt to lose
definitions.meaning: the money left in a bank account, which a lavish spender soon gets through

explanation.surface: A spendthrift tends to lose their poise.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadiness or evenness is equilibrium; the sum remaining in an account is what a big spender runs down.

clue.text: The most renowned of many capital English spanners

definitions.text: The most renowned of many capital English spanners

parts.words: The most renowned of many capital English spanners
parts.note: the best-known of the bridges across the Thames in England's capital

explanation.surface: The finest of England's excellent wrenches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanners' looks like wrenches but means things that span a river, and 'capital' means in the capital as well as excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous crossing over the Thames in the City is the best known of the capital's bridges.
